titleStmt.title: To Harriet Shaw Weaver. Sunday, 10 April 1921
titleStmt.author: James Joyce

seriesStmt.p: Machine readable texts of the unpublished correspondence of James Joyce

projectDesc.p: James Joyce's unpublished correspondence, collected, annotated, and made available as a digital edition

seg.quote: … On receipt of Mr Huebsch’s letter forwarded by you I cabled to Mr Quinn to withdraw the entire typescript of Ulysses

div.p: from Mr Huebsch and all other American publishers and return it to me immediately. Not that I need it but in order to break off relations definitely. Mr Huebsch will not pirate an edition of Ulysses (as he kindly suggested) in the United States but not because of consideration for the writer.

seg.quote: The next day I arranged for a Paris publication to replace the American one – or rather I accepted a proposal made to me by Shakespeare and Co, a bookseller’s here, at the instance of Mr Larbaud.
The actual printing will begin as soon as the number of orders covers approximately the cost of printing

div.p: which they estimate at 20,000 to 25,000 frs though I think it will be more – that is about 150 orders. The manager of Galignani’s library told me that Mr Moore’s new book Heloise published at £4 I think a few weeks ago has now doubled in price. The form of the book is to be carré, the type what they call here no 9 and it will make about 600 pages of that.

seg.quote: This does not cover the English edition but I think it would be to your advantage if that were amalgamated with the Paris one.
… after seven years’ hard labour and in the present exasperated state of my nerves.

div.p: The letter which I enclose was received by me at Christmas. I cabled immediately accepting the conditions and price then have been waiting for the cabled 1000$ which was part of the agreement. It never came & though I cabled and wrote I never received a word in reply to say that the contract was on or off.

seg.quote: It is astonishing to myself that I was able to write as much as I did .…

div.note: Due to fears of prosecution for obscenity, B. W. Huebsch was unwilling to published Ulysses without some alterations to the text. In February 1921, the editors of The Little Review, Margaret Anderson and Jane Heap, were tried for obscenity for publishing the “Nausicaa” episode in their journal’s April 1920 issue. For fuller accounts of “Nausicaa” and the prosecution and trial it occasioned, see JJ to Pound, 24 October 1919, notes; 5 November 1920, notes; and 16 November 1920, notes.
For a fuller account of JJ’s fears that B. W. Huebsch might pirate Ulysses, see JJ to Pound, 5 November 1920, notes.
